questions.question:
In the following question, a sentence is given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives choose the one which best expresses the sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.

The old woman said, “Alas! I have been robbed.

options.text: The old woman exclaimed that she has been robbed.
The old woman exclaimed with joy that she has been robbed.
The old woman exclaimed with sorrow that she has been robbed.
The old woman exclaimed with sorrow that she had been robbed.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4)**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• While changing the narration of an **exclamatory sentence**, we need to follow the given steps-

 
 
• The conjunction **‘that’** should be used in place of a comma (,) and inverted commas (“ ”).
 
• **‘Said’ **will be changed into **exclaimed with sorrow **as **Alas! **is used to express sadness or sorrow.
 
• **1st** **person** (I) is changed into **she** i.e. according to the **subject** of the **reporting** **verb **(old woman).
 
• **Present perfect continuous** (have been) will be changed into **past perfect continuous **(had been).
 
 

The correct sentence- *The old woman exclaimed with sorrow that she had been robbed.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In exclamatory sentences, **direct speech** is changed into **indirect speech** as follows-

 
 
• Said, “What! / “How! Exclaimed
 
• Said, “Wow! / “Hurray! Exclaimed with joy
 
• Said, “Alas! Exclaimed with sorrow
 
• Said, “Fi! / “Ugh! Exclaimed with disgust/ despise
 
• Said, “Oh! Exclaimed with regret/ surprise
 
• Said, “Bravo! / “Well done Applauded + object + saying + that

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that rectifies the underlined group of words in the given sentence.

The committee members argued that the proposed legislation, despite its noble intentions,__ **would eventually undermine their own**__ authority over the local municipalities.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. would eventually undermine its own .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence discusses the consequences of the proposed legislation.
 
• The subject of the sentence is "the proposed legislation," which is singular, so the possessive pronoun must align with the singular subject.
 
• The correct possessive pronoun for a singular subject is "its," not "their" or "it's" (which is a contraction for "it is").
 
• Additionally, the use of "would" is appropriate to indicate a hypothetical or possible outcome in the future.

Correct sentence: *The committee members argued that the proposed legislation, despite its noble intentions, **would eventually undermine its own** authority over the local municipalities.*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Grammar Explanation:**

 
 
• "Would" is used to express hypothetical or expected outcomes.
 
• "Its" is a singular possessive pronoun, used to show ownership for singular subjects.
 
• "Their" is a plural possessive pronoun, which does not match with the singular subject "legislation."
 
• "It's" is incorrect in this context because it is a contraction meaning "it is," which does not fit grammatically.
 
 
 
• **Usage:**

 
 
• The corrected sentence aligns with grammatical rules and ensures clarity in meaning.
 
• Proper pronoun usage strengthens the sentence's coherence.

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

(1) Had the research consortium not been so diligent in their cross-referencing of the longitudinal data / (2) acquired during the clinical trials of the experimental neuro-regenerative serum, / (3) the subtle discrepancies in the patients cognitive recovery / (4) would have likely been overlooked, resulting in a significantly different conclusion.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. the subtle discrepancies in the patients cognitive recovery .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence describes a hypothetical past scenario, and the correct conditional structure to use is the** third conditional**.
 
• The third conditional structure is **"If + Past Perfect, would have + past participle"**, as it refers to unreal past situations.
 
• While the sentence is mostly correct, the phrase "**the subtle discrepancies in the patients cognitive recovery**" contains an error in punctuation. The apostrophe placement suggests plural possessive, which is correct since it refers to multiple patients.

Correct sentence: *Had the research consortium not been so diligent in their cross-referencing of the longitudinal data acquired during the clinical trials of the experimental neuro-regenerative serum, the subtle discrepancies in the **patients**' cognitive recovery would have likely been overlooked, resulting in a significantly different conclusion.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1st Conditional Sentence:**

 
 
• **Structure:** If + Present Simple, will + base verb.
 
• **Example:** If it rains, we will cancel the picnic.
 
• **Usage:** Describes real or possible situations in the future with likely outcomes.
 
 
 
• **2nd Conditional Sentence:**
 
 
• **Structure:** If + Past Simple, would + base verb.
 
• **Example:** If I were rich, I would travel the world.
 
• **Usage:** Describes hypothetical or unreal situations in the present or future.
 
 
 
• **3rd Conditional Sentence:**
 
 
• **Structure:** If + Past Perfect, would have + past participle.
 
• **Example:** If she had studied harder, she would have passed the exam.
 
• **Usage:** Refers to unreal past situations and their imagined outcomes.

questions.question:
Identify the voice of the following sentence:

*"The logistical sector is the silent engine of the Indian economy..."*
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To identify the **voice**, we analyze whether the subject is performing the action or receiving it.
 
• In the sentence: *"The **logistical sector** (Subject) **is** (Linking Verb) the **silent engine** (Subject Complement)..."*
 
• This is a **declarative sentence** using a linking verb ("is"). In English grammar, sentences that describe a state of being or where the subject is the "doer" (or the "being") are classified as **Active Voice**.
 
• Unlike the passive voice, there is no be + V3 (past participle) construction, and the subject is not being acted upon by an external agent.
 
• Why other options are incorrect:
 
 
• **Option 2:** **Passive Voice** requires a V3 form and usually an agent introduced by "by" (e.g., "The economy is driven by the logistical sector").
 
• **Option 3:** **Causative Voice** indicates the subject is causing something to happen through another person or thing (e.g., "The government had the sector modernize").
 
• **Option 4:** **Reflexive Voice** involves the subject and object being the same person or thing (e.g., "The sector reformed itself").
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **1**.

 

**Analytical Insight:** *In high-level competitive exams, simple "State of Being" sentences (using is/am/are/was/were) are categorized under Active Voice because the subject remains the primary focus and starting point of the statement without being a recipient of a past action.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Active Voice:** The subject performs the action or exists in a state.
 
• **Hamstrung:** Severely restricted the efficiency or effectiveness of something.
 
• **Lead Time:** The time between the initiation and completion of a production process.
 
• **Silos:** Isolated systems, departments, or groups that do not communicate with others.

questions.question:
Identify the part of speech of the word "integrating" as used in the following sentence:

*"...aims to rectify this imbalance by integrating disparate digital systems..."*
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To identify the **part of speech**, we analyze how the word "integrating" functions in the sentence: *"...aims to rectify this imbalance **by integrating** disparate digital systems..."*
 
• The word **"by"** is a preposition. In English grammar, a verb ending in *-ing* that follows a preposition and acts as the object of that preposition is a **Gerund**.
 
• A **Gerund** is a verb form that functions as a **noun**. In this case, "integrating" represents the **action or process** of combining systems.
 
• Why other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• **Option 2:** An **Adverb** modifies a verb or adjective (e.g., "The systems were integrated *seamlessly*").
 
• **Option 3:** A **Participle** (specifically a present participle) acts as an adjective to describe a noun or to form continuous tenses (e.g., "The *integrating* software is efficient"). Here, it follows a preposition, marking it as a noun-equivalent (Gerund).
 
• **Option 4:** An **Adjective** describes a noun. While participles can be adjectives, "integrating" here is the object of the preposition "by," not a direct descriptor of a noun.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **1**.

 

**Analytical Insight:** *In high-level competitive exams, distinguishing between Gerunds and Participles is a common challenge. A reliable rule of thumb: if the $V+ing$ follows a preposition (in, at, by, with, for), it is functioning as a **Gerund**.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gerund:** A verb form which functions as a noun, ending in -ing.
 
• **Disparate:** Essentially different in kind; not allowing comparison.
 
• **Rectify:** To put something right; correct.
 
• **Multimodal:** Involving several different modes of activity or transportation.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest is the main "friction point" in India's current logistics?

options.text: The lack of high-speed rail connectivity for passengers.
The high cost of labor in the manufacturing sector.
Fragmented documentation and inter-state regulatory hurdles.
A global decline in the demand for Indian-made exports.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To identify the "friction points," we examine the second paragraph: **"Inter-state checkpoints and fragmented documentation processes have long served as friction points that hemorrhage economic potential."**
 
• The passage emphasizes that modernizing logistics isn't just about physical infrastructure ("laying tarmac or tracks") but about overcoming **regulatory and administrative barriers**.
 
• The goal of policies like **Gati Shakti** and **NLP** is to break these "silos" and synchronize planning to remove these specific hurdles.
 
• Why other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• **Option 1:** The passage focuses on **freight and commodity movement** (logistics), not passenger rail connectivity.
 
• **Option 2:** Labor costs are not mentioned as a friction point; the high cost mentioned is the **logistical cost** (14% of GDP).
 
• **Option 4:** The passage suggests that improving logistics will *enhance* the allure for global supply chains, implying that the current issue is internal efficiency, not a global decline in demand.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **3**.

 

**Analytical Insight:** *In high-level exams, look for "Cause and Effect" keywords. The word **"friction"** in physics prevents smooth motion; similarly, in economics, it refers to things that slow down the "flow" of goods. The passage identifies documentation and checkpoints as these specific slow-down factors.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Silos:** Isolated systems or departments that operate independently without sharing information.
 
• **Gati Shakti:** A National Master Plan in India for multi-modal connectivity to integrated infrastructure.
 
• **IoT-enabled:** Technology that uses the "Internet of Things" to track and share data in real-time.
 
• **Trajectory:** The path followed by an object or, in this case, the predicted growth path of the economy.

questions.question:
**Direction: Choose the option that best transforms the sentence into its other voice:**

Rural spending is undertaken at various levels in the government.

options.text: The government is undertaking rural spending at various levels.
The government undertakes rural spending at various levels.
At various levels rural spending is undertaken by the government.
At various levels rural spending undertakes the government.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'****The government undertakes rural spending at various levels.'** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• The given sentence is in Passive Voice and Simple Present tense. 
 
• As per the given question we have to change it into Active Voice. 
 
• The structure of the given sentence is as follows:
 
 
• Subject (objective case)+ is/am/were + V3 + Object (subjective case). (Passive Voice)
 
• Subject + V1(s/es)+ Object. (Active Voice)
 
 
 
• **Example:**
 
 
• *Their cousin show them some rare photographs. (Active Voice)*
 
• *They are shown some rare photographs by their cousin. (Passive Voice)*
 
 
 
• The subject of the given sentence is 'Rural spending' and the object is 'the government'. 
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject.
 
• The constant object in the given sentence is** "at various levels."**
 
• And 'is undertaken' will be changed into 'undertakes'. 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 2.'

Correct sentence: *The government undertakes rural spending at various levels.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

The bear didn't attack the lady because he was afraid ______ her.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'of'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct preposition to use after the adjective '**afraid**' is '**of**.' The phrase '**afraid of**' is used when someone fears something or someone.
 
• Thus, in the blank, the correct phrase to complete the sentence is '**afraid of her**.'
 
• Options 'at,' 'as,' and 'for' do not fit grammatically or logically in this sentence.
 
• Given the sentence and the intended connotation, the preposition '**of**' is the only valid option to use after '**afraid**'.
 
• **Correct Sentence:** *The bear didn’t attack the lady because he was afraid **of **her.*

Therefore, the correct answer is **'Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 'Afraid at her' (Option 2) is grammatically incorrect. We do not use 'at' after 'afraid' in English.
 
• Similarly, 'Afraid as her' (Option 3) is incorrect. 'As' is used to compare similar things or statements, but 'afraid as her' does not make sense in this context.
 
• 'Afraid for her' (Option 4) could be used in a different context, but not in this sentence. 'Afraid for someone' means being fearful for another person's safety, not being scared of that person themselves.

__

• The article** "an"** should be used before words starting with a vowel sound, but **"rose" **starts with a consonant sound.

questions.question:
**Which of following best expresses the idiom given in capital words in the sentence, **

'Reena is a kind of a person WHO WEARS HEART ON HER SLEEVE'.?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'expresses her emotions openly'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **WHO WEARS HEART ON HER SLEEVE **is an idiom that means** you openly show your feelings or emotions rather than keeping them hidden.**

 
 
• **​Example - ***I can tell Jenny is upset; she **wears her heart on her sleeve**.*
 
 
 
• So, **expresses her emotions openly **is the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
 
• Hence, **option 3 **is the correct answer. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **Mistake Points__** 

 
• **Option 3 **which states '**Expresses her emotions freely**' may seem like the correct answer but there is a subtle difference between the words **'openly' and 'freely'**. 
 
• **Openly **means without concealment, deception, or prevarication, especially where these might be expected; frankly or honestly.
 
• **Freely **means not under the control of another; as one wishes.
 
• Thus, **expressing emotions openly **is more appropriate as the meaning of the given idiom.

questions.question:
**Direction: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. We do not, then, limit our thinking to our own caste or religion but think about all our fellow citizens.

B. National integration is the feeling among all the citizens of a country that they all are part of one nation.

C. It helps us to develop a broad perspective that all of us together constitute an extensive group called ‘the nation’.

D. This feeling takes up beyond the bounds of family, caste, religion as well as region.

E. This feeling of an extensive group gives rise to a fellow feeling, a feeling of brotherhood amongst the citizens.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**BDCEA**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let's look at the sequence of the sentence.
 
 
• **Statement B** is the opening of the sentence as it introduces the subject and theme of the passage which is 'National integration is the feeling among all the citizens of a country that they all are part of one nation'.
 
• **Statement D** is the second statement of the sentence as it adds more by telling us that the feeling of National integration takes up beyond the bounds of family, caste, religion as well as region.
 
• **Statement C** is the third statement of the sentence as it continues further information that by taking up beyond the bounds of family, caste, religion and region it helps us to develop a broad perspective that all of us together constitute an extensive group called ‘the nation’.
 
• **Statement E** is the fourth statement of the sentence as it tells us that this feeling of an extensive group called 'nation' gives rise to a fellow feeling, a feeling of brotherhood amongst the citizens.
 
• **Statement A** is the fifth statement of the sentence as it concludes the passage as a citizen of a fellow nation we do not, then, limit our thinking to our own caste or religion but think about all our fellow citizens.
 
 

Hence, the correct answer is **option (2).**

**Correct sequence:__**

 
• B. National integration is the feeling among all the citizens of a country that they all are part of one nation.
 
• D. This feeling takes up beyond the bounds of family, caste, religion as well as region.
 
• C. It helps us to develop a broad perspective that all of us together constitute an extensive group called ‘the nation’.
 
• E. This feeling of an extensive group gives rise to a fellow feeling, a feeling of brotherhood amongst the citizens.
 
• A. We do not, then, limit our thinking to our own caste or religion but think about all our fellow citizens.

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

Were you serving the beautiful princesses of great Ireland?

options.text: Were the beautiful princesses of great Ireland being served by you?
Were the beautiful princesses of great Ireland served by you?
Were the beautiful princesses of great Ireland been served by you?
Was the beautiful princesses of great Ireland being served by you?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Were the beautiful princesses of great Ireland being served by you?"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• This is an example of the **past continuous tense.**
 
• Rules for this type of conversion:
 
 
• Acti**ve: ****Was/Were + subject + Verb ing form + object ?**
 
• **Passive: Was/Were + object + being + V-III + by + Subject?**
 
 
 
• While comparing with the basic structure:
 
 
• you(subject)
 
• serve(verb)
 
• the beautiful princesses of great Ireland(object)
 
 

Hence the correct answer: *Were the beautiful princesses of great Ireland being served by you?*

questions.question:
Given below are some idioms/phrases followed by four alternative meanings to each. Choose the response (a), (b), (c) or (d) which is the most appropriate expression and mark your response in the Answer Sheet accordingly.

Queer the pitch

options.text: To make things more confusing rather than giving a clarification
To ruin something planned, arranged, or attempted
To unintentionally give somebody an advantage over the competitors
To produce something in such large quantities that competing products suffer

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**To ruin something planned, arranged, or attempted**.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• If someone/something 'queers the/someone's pitch' means that **the person/thing spoils or interferes in order to make it difficult for someone to do something that they had planned to do**.

 
 
• For example, *Virat Kohli **was just going to the crease when some people from the opponent's audience box started shouting in an attempt **to queer the pitch***. 
 
 
 
• So, the correct meaning of the idiom '*Queer the pitch*'*** ***is **To ruin something planned, arranged, or attempted**.

*Hence, the correct answer is **Option 2**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 'Queer' when used as a verb means 'to spoil.' The phrase, a British term came into existence as slang during the 19th century. The pitch used in the phrase referred to the place where a street performer stationed themselves or the site of a market trader's stall. Putting those two together we get the meaning of this little phrase.

questions.question: ______ a national holiday tomorrow.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2) It's**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"It's" **is the contraction of** "it is," **which grammatically suits the sentence to state that tomorrow is a national holiday.

• **Its: Possessive form of "it,"** not suitable for expressing a state of being or fact about time.
 
• **There’s:** The contraction for "there is," which could potentially be used but is less direct in this context than "It's."
 
• **Will be:** While it also indicates the future, the simple present "it's" is more straightforward for stating facts or scheduled events
